result:
The task is finished — the memo was submitted and accepted, so there's nothing further to request. Here's the wrap-up:

## March revenue recognition — posted and documented

**Entries (US, 2026-03-31, all with support attached)**

| JE | Entry | Amount | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| JE-00311 | Dr 2200 / Cr 4000 | $4,000 | Dunmore core subscription, $48,000 ÷ 12 |
| JE-00312 | Dr 2200 / Cr 4000 | $1,000 | Dunmore Analytics module, $10,000 ÷ 10 (Mar–Dec) |
| JE-00313 | Dr 1300 / Cr 4100 | $5,000 | Harlow Freight, 50,000 shipments × $0.10 |

**Key judgment — Dunmore amendment.** Amendment No. 1 adds a *distinct* service priced at its *standalone selling price*, so under ASC 606-10-25-12 it's a separate contract, not a modification of the existing one. That means no reallocation of the core price and no catch-up — the core stays at $4,000/month and Analytics runs at $1,000/month from March.

**Harlow Freight.** Usage-based, satisfied per shipment, invoiced quarterly in arrears → March earned usage goes to 1300 Unbilled Receivables, consistent with Jan/Feb treatment.

**Tie-out.** 2200 ends at $45,000 (36,000 core + 9,000 Analytics) and 1300 at $13,600 (Harlow Q1) — both agree exactly to the contracts. No approval requests needed (each entry < $10,000; the two Dunmore entries are genuinely separate contracts, not a split). No exceptions flagged. US "Revenue recognition" checklist item marked complete.

**One follow-up for April:** when the Harlow Q1 invoice is issued, it should clear 1300 (Dr 1100 / Cr 1300 $13,600) rather than hit revenue again.
